Hi Janelle — thanks for sending these over and for the heads up. Forwarding to Procurement and Payments (Ben, Laura) to confirm the PO path. A couple quick Qs so we can move fast:

- Is the W-8BEN-E signed under the legal entity that will appear on invoices? If AquaPoint will bill from multiple subsidiaries, list which entity wants the PO.
- Do you have a short attestation confirming AquaPoint is the beneficial owner for Redwood payments (one sentence is fine) or do you expect to remain an intermediary withholding agent?

If Procurement can provision a conditional PO today, Finance will require either the attestation or a statement on company letterhead that clarifies withholding status. Ben/Laura — can you advise whether a provisional PO split (one PO per billing entity) is supported, or do we need a single PO for now?

Thanks — I’ll stand by.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Janelle — quick procurement note from Payments:

- If the W-8BEN-E shows AquaPoint as the beneficial owner and the signed name matches the invoicing entity, we can issue a standard PO.
- If AquaPoint is billing from multiple legal entities, we prefer separate POs per remit-to entity to avoid cross-entity tax complications. We can create PO AP-449 as a conditional split: AP-449A (AquaPoint US Inc.) + AP-449B (AquaPoint EU Services) — production of the second PO will require the matching W-8/W-9 for that entity.

Action items for Janelle to unblock PO issuance:
1) Confirm invoicing entity exactly as it will appear on invoices (legal name + EIN or TIN where applicable).
2) Provide a one-line attestation that AquaPoint is the beneficial owner for Redwood payments (signed or on company letterhead).
3) If you want the PO split, indicate the second billing entity and send the additional tax form for that entity.

We can provision a provisional PO (valid for 30 days) once items 1+2 are received. Laura, please confirm SLA for creating provisional PO after receipt.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Vendor Onboarding — Procurement
Redwood Inference
